comment: Derived from the BodyParts3D 4.0 99%-reduced OBJ set by
tools/build-bd-template.mjs. Not hand-authored; every number here is a
measurement on the source meshes. Attribution ships with the assets:

source.holder: The Database Center for Life Science (DBCLS)
source.attribution: BodyParts3D, (c) The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan

frame.space: LAS millimetres: +x subject left, +y anterior, +z superior

precision.rule: largest d with min(level height, clock-sector arc at the skin, radial half) / 2^d >= the skin mesh mean edge length

declarations.summary: At the listed levels and azimuths, the first skin crossing is a limb surface, not the trunk surface, so `r = 1` there is the outside of the arm or thigh.
declarations.why: A limb lying against the trunk leaves no skin between them, so there is no trunk surface to find along those rays. The radius is the honest distance to the skin and the frame stays exactly invertible; only the anatomical reading of `r = 1` changes.
declarations.detection: A ray is flagged when it crosses the humerus or the femur before reaching the skin, then the witnessed azimuths are dilated by 3 knot(s) either way (15 degrees).
declarations.completeness: SOUND, NOT COMPLETE. A ray through limb soft tissue only, lateral or anterior to the bone, is not witnessed, so the published arc is a lower bound on the affected azimuths.
declarations.fix: Needs a trunk-only surface. BodyParts3D publishes one skin concept for the whole body, so this source cannot supply it; a different surface source would remove the declaration without changing any address already issued.

declarations.summary: The whole fused sacrum is one addressable level, 133.5 mm tall against a 25.9 mm median — 5.2x. Sacral addressing is correspondingly coarse in the axial direction.
declarations.why: docs/alc-1-admissibility.md §2 measured the alternative: cutting the fused sacrum into short levels is strictly worse at every girth, because each cut both shortens the chord and tightens the turn, and the sacral concavity faces the deep pelvis where there is a lot of tissue. Five sacral levels put 1.2-3.2% of body volume inside a fold.
declarations.detection: Structural. S02-S05 are reserved grammar and are realised by no template.
declarations.completeness: Exact. This is a property of the level set, not an estimate.
declarations.fix: Not a defect to fix. A finer sacral frame can be added later without a breaking change because S02-S05 are reserved, but it needs the non-tubular pelvic parameterisation rather than more slabs of the same kind.

levels.note: axis from the measured S1 endplate: admissibility §5 requirement 2
